decision_context: An occupying power is preparing and beginning a coordinated roundup of a legally targeted minority in a neighbouring occupied country. The plan has been credibly leaked, members of the minority are going into hiding, and a short sea crossing offers a practical escape route to a nearby neutral state. The neutral state must decide whether to make clear that refugees from the targeted group and close relatives will be admitted rather than turned away.
decision_question: Should the neutral state offer temporary sanctuary to members of the targeted minority and close relatives fleeing the imminent roundup and deportation operation?
actors: its border, maritime and refugee authorities
available_actions: Offer temporary sanctuary to the targeted minority and close relatives who can reach the neutral state during the emergency.
Keep existing entry policy without a special guarantee and decide individual arrivals case by case.
Limit admission to selected categories or a small fixed quota.
Refuse admission to minimise resource, security and diplomatic risks associated with neutrality.

affected_parties.party: Members of the targeted minority facing imminent group-based arrest and deportation
affected_parties.known_interests_or_risks: Liberty, family unity, safety from forced deportation and access to a reachable neutral refuge.
Family unity, safety and ability to remain with endangered relatives.

affected_parties.party: Residents and public institutions of the neutral state
affected_parties.known_interests_or_risks: Resources, accommodation, security, public administration and domestic stability during wartime.
Neutrality, relations with belligerent powers, national security, humanitarian responsibility and control over admission policy.

affected_parties.party: People in the occupied country helping the endangered group escape
affected_parties.known_interests_or_risks: Whether a viable destination exists and their own risks if escape attempts fail.

known_evidence.claim: Occupation/security authorities are preparing and beginning a coordinated operation to arrest members of the targeted minority and deport them from the occupied country.
Many members of the minority are going into hiding and need a destination outside the occupier's control if they are to evade arrest.
The neutral state is geographically close and can be reached from the occupied country by small boats across a narrow sea passage.
The neutral state controls whether refugees reaching its territory are admitted and protected or refused entry.
Admission would create real but bounded administrative, accommodation and wartime-security responsibilities.
A communicated willingness to admit refugees would materially increase the feasibility of escape by giving rescuers and endangered families a known safe destination.
Refusing admission or leaving entry materially uncertain risks closing the most accessible neutral refuge available during the imminent roundup.
The threatened people are targeted because of group identity rather than an individualised finding that each committed a harmful act.

known_uncertainties: How many refugees will arrive if sanctuary is offered.
How the occupying power will respond diplomatically or operationally.
How long refuge will be required.
The precise treatment people will face after deportation, although forced arrest and deportation themselves create immediate severe loss of liberty and safety.
The resources required for reception and support.
known_alternatives: Offer temporary emergency sanctuary with security screening that does not defeat urgent access to safety.
Admit this specific endangered population without making a broader unlimited refugee commitment.
Coordinate reception with rescue networks to reduce maritime and administrative risk.
Keep policy ambiguous or restrictive, leaving refugees uncertain whether arrival will result in protection.
requested_output: Assess whether the neutral state has a positive moral duty to provide a feasible sanctuary when severe group-based harm is imminent nearby.
Weigh legitimate neutrality, security and resource interests without assuming they automatically override endangered people's safety.
Assess whether bounded temporary admission is proportionate.
Consider the moral consequences of refusal or passivity as well as action.
Give a Moral Code assessment using only this packet and without identifying the historical case.
